steps.what: Define promotions for current programs and specials using verified programme facts
Draft promotional copy and outline creative treatments for the selected programs

loop.purpose: Draft promotional wording from the director's defined concept and checked facts
loop.input: Checked promotion brief with programme version, allowed claims, tone and length
loop.output: Draft copy and treatment options with fact references
loop.check: Director checks every claim, airtime, implied promise, tone and proposed treatment against programme material
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsuitable wording is rewritten manually within this step
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates hold fixed fields but variable creative phrasing needs writing; no loop is used for factual fields

steps.what: Evaluate promotion treatments, refine the chosen version and accept the production brief

tasks.design: Use native templates in {DOCS} for programme facts and a bounded loop for wording around the director's chosen concept. The director checks the draft and accepts a specific production brief; production, rights clearance and broadcast release remain separate work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated copy variants took time even after the promotion's concept and facts were settled.
tasks.enabler_now: Text generation can propose wording from a small checked brief without deciding the campaign's creative purpose.
tasks.still_hard: Appeal, truthful emphasis and fit with the programme and audience remain editorial judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The director knows which promise the programme can actually deliver.
tasks.altitude: Some wording effort falls; concept choice and responsibility for promotional claims stay human.

reach.task: Translate a promotion brief into a feasible treatment

evidence.claim: A constrained text loop can draft promotional wording from supplied facts; the proposed labour savings are unmeasured model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is developing a promotion concept, copy and production brief, excluding shooting, editing, rights acquisition, campaign scheduling and public release. Do not count the same copy draft again in another role.

Programme editors produce programme material through unchanged work. Director creates and verifies programme identifier, exact version, current airtime source, audience, intended message, allowed claims, protected wording, tone and length in s1's 30 hours. No free structured creative brief is assumed.

s2 retains 22.75 hours for checking and rewriting including manual fallback. Missing facts, uncertain airtime or unclear permissions are left unresolved and returned to the director; no invented quotes, endorsements or clearance flags are used.
Try native templates first. Public release is outside the proposal and remains with existing responsible people after production and clearance; no automatic publishing is introduced.
unknowns: How much wording is reusable across current programmes
Which programme facts and assets are cleared for promotional use
research_questions: Does drafting reduce effort after checking programme promises and exact airtimes?

already_counted.description: Check wording and manually rewrite unsuitable suggestions

incremental.description: Maintain brief templates and audit unsupported promotional claims

approvals.approved_version: Exact promotion production brief, copy, treatment and programme fact snapshot; edits void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=87.75, gross=12.25; subtract 6 focal upkeep for central net=6.25. Range assumes frequent manual rewriting and unchanged concept evaluation; no production or public release time is saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Evaluate community needs, ratings and demographics and specify programming and coverage constraints
Place selected programming and event coverage into available broadcast slots
Resolve scheduling conflicts and accept programming and event coverage trade-offs

tasks.design: Configure scheduling constraints in {OTHER}, the broadcast scheduling system, after the director selects programmes and coverage priorities. Generate a candidate schedule, expose conflicts and let the director decide trade-offs before accepting the exact version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated slot placement and duration checks were mixed with editorial planning decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native broadcast scheduling can build playlists against explicit rights, repeat and content constraints.
tasks.still_hard: Community relevance and audience needs do not reduce to maximising a ratings score.
tasks.human_edge: The director balances public value, audience expectations and production feasibility.
tasks.altitude: Less mechanical slot placement; programme selection and audience judgement remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Production lead times and live-event uncertainty

evidence.claim: Mediagenix Scheduling Automation builds playlists while checking rights, repeat limits and content rules.
The proposed division of human planning and fixed slot placement, including savings, is an unmeasured model scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is planning and accepting a programme and event coverage schedule, excluding creating programmes, booking resources, live timing monitoring and completed-log review. Assign overlapping comparisons once.

Catalogue and rights staff produce identifiers, verified durations, available versions and rights-window references through normal work; event producers provide event windows and existing feasibility advice. Extra metadata upkeep is counted below, and missing source fields do not become free automated classifications.

Director creates the checked scheduling specification in s1's 35 hours: selected programme versions, channel, slot windows, durations, hard constraints, permitted repeats, verified rights references, event windows and editorial priority order. Audience interpretation, constraint choice and capture are retained human effort.

The machine only places the director's selected items under explicit rules. Unknown rights, incompatible timings or infeasible constraints stop generation and return to manual planning in s3; it never silently relaxes editorial constraints.
Try native scheduling first. s3 retains conflict negotiation, source checks and exact-version acceptance; broadcasting and external bookings remain existing downstream work.
unknowns: How complete programme duration and rights metadata are
Whether native constraints cover local event coverage requirements
research_questions: Can native scheduling reproduce a past accepted schedule without silently relaxing its constraints?

already_counted.description: Capture explicit constraints, resolve conflicts and accept the schedule

incremental.description: Maintain scheduling rules and test changed constraints
Maintain additional catalogue and rights reference fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact schedule version, selected programme versions, rights references and resolved conflicts; changes require renewed acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25; minus 8 focal upkeep gives central net=17. Range assumes partial native coverage and frequent manual event adjustments. Four other-role hours are recorded separately; audience analysis and negotiations keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Specify network transmission sources and advisory routing for daily schedules and special feeds
Monitor named network channels and collect matching advisories and program changes
Read advisories, confirm transmission meaning and determine schedule or content responses

tasks.design: Use native subscriptions in {OTHER}, the network advisory reception system, to collect source notices and notify the director through {EMAIL}. Matching uses explicit feed metadata; interpretation and any schedule or content response remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly watching several advisory channels could delay noticing a relevant change.
tasks.enabler_now: Where networks provide timestamped advisory messages, native subscriptions can collect and route them without interpreting their content.
tasks.still_hard: An advisory's relevance and consequences may depend on changing local schedules or incomplete network information.
tasks.human_edge: The director confirms the meaning of a network change and coordinates a suitable response.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated channel polling where structured notices exist; response authority is unchanged.

reach.task: Confirm feed changes and reception problems
reach.learn: Network advisory conventions and transmission verification

evidence.claim: Explicit metadata subscriptions can route network notices without interpreting them; applicability and proposed hours are model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is noticing and assessing network advisories, excluding generating the underlying schedule, completed-log checking and implementing transmission changes.

OTHER means network advisory reception software. Network operators produce advisory identifier, issue timestamp, source channel or feed identifier, message body and effective time through their normal notice publication after s1 and before s2. Savings require a supported message feed; voice-only or screen-only transmissions remain fully manual and earn no polling saving.

Director produces and verifies source identifiers, local channel mapping, monitored periods, duty contact, duplicate key and stale-feed interval in s1's 25 hours. No free discrepancy or importance code is assumed; routing is source based, not semantic.

Missing metadata or stale feeds trigger visible failure status and manual channel monitoring in s3, whose 55 hours retain reading, checking and response decisions. Additional local reception-field upkeep is counted below.
Test native subscriptions before custom integration. The queue does not alter schedules, acknowledge editorial clearance or authorize a broadcast.
unknowns: Whether each network provides a reliable supported advisory feed
How often advisories require watching or listening to an unstructured transmission
research_questions: Does a native subscription deliver notices and detect stale feeds without missing notices found by manual monitoring?

already_counted.description: Capture routing fields, read advisories and handle manual monitoring exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain routing and test feed failure notifications

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20; subtract 7 focal upkeep for central net=13. Range applies only where structured notice feeds cover part of polling; unstructured transmissions remain manual. Two other-role upkeep hours are recorded outside focal savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Explore audience interests and station capabilities for potential programs and features
Develop distinctive ideas for programs and features the station could produce

tasks.design: Keep programme ideation human and record concepts in {DOCS}. The director connects audience interests with the station's capabilities and develops a distinctive editorial premise.
tasks.previous_blocker: The main difficulty is finding a worthwhile premise rather than producing a list of plausible titles.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native idea records are sufficient; no new automated drafting is proposed for creative development.
tasks.still_hard: Originality, local relevance and a programme's potential emerge through exploration and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The director recognises an overlooked story and understands why the station should tell it.
tasks.altitude: Ideation time and creative responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Develop a programme premise into a feasible format
reach.learn: Editorial concept development and production feasibility

evidence.claim: Developing station-specific programme ideas requires creative and contextual judgement; no labour saving is claimed for generating generic suggestions.

assumptions: Boundary is exploring and developing new programme concepts, excluding selecting finished material, detailed scheduling, audience research collection and producing the programme. Count shared creative development once.

Audience contacts and station colleagues provide accounts of interests and capabilities through normal discussion. Director elicits and checks these in s1's retained time and creates concepts in s2; no structured demand score or free captured creative brief is assumed.
Keep current native idea records. No additional system, capture requirement or process means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which audiences the station currently understands poorly
What production constraints limit concept development
research_questions: Can each concept explain its intended audience, editorial purpose and feasible production approach?

already_counted.description: Explore interests and develop original programme concepts

incremental.description: No changed process or new upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Audience discussion and creative development retain their full effort; generic suggestion generation is not treated as completed ideation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Native tools can reduce routine schedule placement and supported advisory polling, while creative concepts, promotional claims and editorial choices remain human.
reach: Work with producers on creative feasibility
Work with broadcast technicians on advisory reception and timing evidence
skills_to_grow: Check promotional promises against programme facts
Recognise missing or stale advisory feeds
role.ambitious_version: Plan relevant programming with traceable constraints and dependable notice handling while preserving human creative and editorial responsibility.
